title: private-deploy-networking-incident-breadcrumbs
content:
Summary:
- Notes + breadcrumbs while debugging customer private deployment networking failures (VPC peering + DNS + TLS + egress).
- Initial customer report: Private deployment endpoints occasionally time out when calling the control plane (hosted) and also failing mutual TLS to our admin LB.
- First seen after customer applied VPC peering updates on 2026-03-02. Intermittent failures, worse during higher traffic.

Timeline / quick timeline of events:
- 2026-03-02 09:12 UTC: Customer applied VPC peering + added route to peer for 10.20.0.0/16 -> peer-abc123 (ticket INC-2026-045).
- 2026-03-02 10:05 UTC: First errors reported (timeouts to control-plane-api.redwood.host).
- 2026-03-02 11:00-13:00 UTC: Repro attempts; saw both successful and failed connections from customer pod to control plane.
- 2026-03-03 02:30 UTC: Customer rolled back one NACL rule; no clear improvement.
- 2026-03-04 07:20 UTC: I started a deeper trace (notes below).

What I observed (high level):
- Intermittent TCP connection timeouts to control-plane endpoints (443).
- DNS resolution sometimes returned internal IPs (private hosted zone) and other times returned public IPs - looks like split-horizon/different VPC association behavior.
- When DNS pointed to private IP, traffic failed (tcp handshake stalls). When DNS resolved to public, TLS completed and request succeeded but route sometimes misrouted back into the customer's VPC causing asymmetric routing.
- TLS handshake errors occasionally: "SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure" and "certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain" in some mutual-TLS setups.

Commands I ran (copy/paste for reproducibility) and outputs:
- From affected pod (kubectl exec into app pod):
  - nslookup control-plane-api.redwood.host
    Server: 10.0.0.2
    Address: 10.0.0.2#53

    Non-authoritative answer:
    Name: control-plane-api.redwood.host
    Address: 172.31.45.12

  - dig +short control-plane-api.redwood.host @10.0.0.2
    172.31.45.12

  - curl -v https://control-plane-api.redwood.host/health --resolve control-plane-api.redwood.host:443:172.31.45.12
    * TCP_NODELAY set
    * Connected to 172.31.45.12 (172.31.45.12) port 443 (#0)
    * TLS 1.2 connection (cipher AES128-GCM-SHA256)
    * SSL connection using TLSv1.2 / ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
    HTTP/1.1 200 OK

  - curl -v https://control-plane-api.redwood.host/health
    * Trying 54.210.12.34...
    * TCP_NODELAY set
    * connect to 54.210.12.34 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
    * Failed to connect to control-plane-api.redwood.host port 443: Connection timed out

- traceroute (from a bastion in the customer's VPC to 172.31.45.12):
  traceroute to 172.31.45.12 (172.31.45.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
   1  10.20.1.1 (10.20.1.1)  1.118 ms  1.047 ms  1.006 ms
   2  10.30.0.1 (10.30.0.1)  2.125 ms  2.063 ms  2.013 ms
   3  * * *
   4  100.64.0.10 (100.64.0.10)  10.234 ms  10.191 ms  10.152 ms
   5  172.31.45.12 (172.31.45.12)  12.400 ms  12.360 ms  12.320 ms
  - Intermittent hops with * suggest ECMP/asymmetric routes or transient blackholing.

- iptables / sysctl checks on pod node (asked node-ops team for output):
  - iptables -L -n | grep 172.31.45.12 => no explicit DROP rules.
  - sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1 (enabled)

- tcpdump (short capture during a failed attempt):
  - tcpdump -n host 172.31.45.12 and port 443 -c 50
    12:20:01.123456 IP 10.20.1.45.43122 > 172.31.45.12.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 29200, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
    12:20:01.123789 IP 172.31.45.12.443 > 10.20.1.45.43122: Flags [S.], seq 54321, ack 12346, win 28960, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 456 ecr 123], length 0
    12:20:01.124000 IP 10.20.1.45.43122 > 172.31.45.12.443: Flags [R], seq 12346, win 0, length 0
  - Client (pod) sends R after SYN-ACK - indicates client stack sending R (reset) shortly after receiving SYN-ACK; could be local firewall, conntrack, or kernel-level R due to missing route for return path.

- openssl s_client tests (to public IP):
  - openssl s_client -connect control-plane-api.redwood.host:443 -servername control-plane-api.redwood.host
    CONNECTED(00000003)
    140735...:error:1408A0C1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher
    ---
    no peer certificate available
  - When connecting directly to public IP sometimes handshake fails with 'no shared cipher' (likely SNI / ALPN / cipher policy mismatch on our side or customer's outbound TLS inspection).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Split-horizon DNS / Private hosted zone mis-association
   - Evidence: nslookup sometimes returns private IPs, sometimes public. Customer's Route 53 private zone might be associated with an overlapping VPC (maybe multiple VPCs) and records are being resolved inconsistently depending on the DNS server used (node resolver vs pod resolver).
   - Impact: traffic sometimes tries to go over peering to private IP that doesn't have symmetric return path, causing resets/timeouts.

2) Asymmetric routing due to missing route propagation on peering or missing return routes from our side into the customer's subnets
   - Evidence: traceroute with intermittent * and tcpdump showing client R after SYN-ACK. Could be a router along the path rewrites/blackholes.

3) NACL or security-group/NAT translation causing intermittent resets at scale
   - Evidence: failures worse under higher traffic; NACLs are stateless and could drop ephemeral port return traffic if misconfigured. Customer changed NACL around time of peering update.

4) TLS/mTLS mismatch (SNI/cipher mismatch or TLS proxy)
   - Evidence: openssl errors (no shared cipher) and occasional cert validation errors. Customer mentioned they recently added an egress proxy/inspection appliance that re-terminates TLS (could present different certs).

5) Conntrack / ephemeral port exhaustion on the pod/node or on a NAT gateway
   - Evidence: client sending R after SYN-ACK can be caused by conntrack TTL/entries being wrong, or NAT gateway dropping replies. Under load, NAT could run out of ports.

Immediate checks to run (next time we reproduce):
- From pod and node: dig +short @<node-resolver> and @<cluster-dns> to compare records and check TTLs.
- Check Route 53 private zone associations: which VPCs? any overlapping CIDRs?
- Validate VPC peering route tables both sides: ensure 10.x -> peer routes present & no overlapping route 0.0.0.0/0 via peer.
- Confirm no policy-based routing causing return traffic to go to a different IGW or NAT.
- Run hping3 to check TCP handshake timing and whether client resets immediately after SYN-ACK consistently.
  - hping3 -S -p 443 172.31.45.12 --fast --count 100
- Check conntrack table sizes on node while reproducing: sudo conntrack -L | wc -l; also check /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max and current usage.
- Check NAT gateway metrics (AWS) for port exhaustion (High ephemeral port allocation).
- Ask customer to temporarily disable egress TLS inspection/proxy to validate 'no shared cipher' errors are caused by MITM.
- Capture full tcpdump on both ends (customer and our edge) to confirm symmetric flows.
- Check our load balancer (admin LB) cipher policy and SNI handling; verify server-side supports expected ciphers and TLS versions.

Possible root cause scenarios (what I'd bet on):
- Primary: DNS split-horizon + VPC peering asymmetry (most likely). The private hosted zone is resolving to internal IPs for some resolvers but not all, causing traffic to attempt private path without proper routing back. That can cause intermittent success/fail depending on which resolver/pod/node handles DNS.
- Secondary: NAT/conntrack exhaustion under load amplifies the problem (why failure rate increases with traffic).
- Tertiary: TLS re-termination (customer egress appliance) causing occasional handshake failures and cert mismatches.

Short-term mitigations (customer-facing):
- Ask customer to force use of public control-plane endpoint for the private deployment temporarily (pin by host override or /etc/hosts in nodes) while we debug. This will route over public internet and avoid peering issues.
- Ask customer to disable any TLS-intercepting proxy for a short window.
- Increase conntrack table / NAT gateway port pool if we see exhaustion (ops action with node-ops/customer cloud team).

Longer-term fixes / checks to schedule:
- Add route-checker playbook to verify peering route tables and route propagation both sides after peering changes.
- Add DNS consistency check as part of onboarding: ensure private hosted zone associations only include intended VPCs; standardize node/pod resolvers to use the same upstream.
- Harden LB cipher support & add diagnostics to surface SNI/cipher mismatches in logs (and correlate with customer IPs).
- Build a small synthetic test that runs every 5 minutes from customer VPC (with customer's consent) to detect asymmetric routing early.

Notes / to-do (my personal):
- TODO: Request full VPC peering config from customer (peering id, route tables snapshots both sides) - opened INC-2026-045 but need attachments.
- TODO: Get node-level tcpdump from customer (point them to the exact tcpdump command).
- TODO: Ask infra team if we've seen similar "client R after SYN-ACK" patterns in other incidents (maybe SRE has a KB).
- TODO: Reproduce with small local VPC peering test in staging with overlapping resolver configs.

Slack snippets (for context):
- Customer message: "after peering we see intermittent 504s to control plane and jobs failing to start. sometimes it works"
- Customer note: "we added an egress proxy appliance yesterday for TLS inspection"

Quick hypotheses to call out to customer when talking:
- "We think DNS split-horizon is returning private IPs to some pods which then attempt to use the peered path; that path is asymmetric or missing return routes, causing resets. Can you confirm which VPCs are associated with the private zone and whether your cluster nodes and pods use the same DNS server?"
- "Separately, please confirm the egress proxy is not intercepting TLS - it can cause cipher/SNI mismatches."

Logs / snippets attached to ticket: (copy these lines into INC-2026-045)
- tcpdump snippet showing client R after SYN-ACK
- curl outputs with both private and public IPs and the differing behaviors
- openssl s_client error lines

If I get more time today:
- Automate a small script to query multiple resolvers in the customer's VPC and print differences (node resolver, pod DNS, kube-dns).
- Coordinate with node-ops to ramp conntrack limits on a test node and reproduce.

End of notes.

-- Noah
(keeping working notes here so folks can jump in, feel free to add comments in ticket INC-2026-045)
